item.title: Add My Supplied Voiceover

exact_text: Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

turns.text: Add a warm, clear English voice-over to this silent clip, saying exactly: “Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.” Keep the video unchanged. No music or captions.

item.tests: Tests adding an exact supplied narration to existing footage rather than returning standalone speech or regenerating the video.

answer_sheet.Voiceover wording: Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.
answer_sheet.Footage, aspect ratio, and duration: Use the attached silent clip, preserving its framing, sequence, and full 10-second duration.
answer_sheet.Lip synchronization: Not requested; leave the existing video unchanged.

must_haves: The deliverable is the attached kitchen-table video with an audible voice-over, not an audio-only file.
The narration says the supplied script exactly, without omissions, substitutions, or extra spoken words.
The entire narration is intelligible and finishes before the 10-second video ends.
The original footage, framing, and sequence remain unchanged.
There is no music or added on-screen text.

turns.text: Could you add a warm, clear English voice-over to the attached silent clip? I’m hoping this will make the morning advice feel a little more approachable. The voice-over should say exactly: “Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.” Please keep the video unchanged, including its framing, sequence, and full 10-second duration. I don’t have a particular voice identity or gender in mind, so that’s your call, and I’m not asking for lip synchronization. Please don’t add any music or captions.

dialog.agent:
I can’t make this exact edit with the connected Magic Hour tools: they don’t offer a way to add narration to an existing clip while keeping its video unchanged. I haven’t modified your file or spent credits.

To preserve your framing, sequence, and full **10-second duration**, this needs a voice-over audio track added in a video editor—not video regeneration or lip sync.

I’d use a warm, conversational English voice at roughly **144 words per minute**, reading exactly:

> Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

No music or captions.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
The blocker isn’t the free plan—it’s that the connected tools don’t have an audio-only overlay function. Trying a video-generation tool could change your visuals rather than simply add the narration.

**Would you accept a regenerated version that may alter the footage?** I’d aim to retain the framing, sequence, and 10-second length, with your exact warm English voice-over and no music, captions, or lip sync—but I couldn’t guarantee unchanged visuals.
dialog.user: Yes, please go ahead and try, though I’m still hoping to preserve the original framing, sequence, and full 10-second duration. Please use the exact narration I provided, with a warm, clear English delivery and no music or captions. I don’t have a particular voice identity or gender in mind, so that part is your call.

dialog.agent:
Before I can start, the generation planner requires these two answers:

- Where will this be shown or posted (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, a website, print, somewhere else)?
- Should any words appear on it? If so, which, exactly?

You’ve already specified no captions; you can simply confirm “no on-screen words” for the second question.
dialog.user: I haven’t specified where it will be shown or posted, so I don’t have a platform to give you. No on-screen words, please—just the exact narration I already provided. I’m still hoping to preserve the original framing, sequence, and full 10-second duration.

dialog.agent:
Understood—no on-screen words, and the original framing and 10-second duration remain the target.

The planner won’t accept “preserve the source aspect ratio” and is repeating this question:

> Where will this be shown or posted (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, a website, print, somewhere else)?

You don’t need to invent a platform. **Do you know the clip’s dimensions or aspect ratio?** That should let me specify its original shape without guessing. Nothing has been generated or charged yet.
dialog.user: ok ok, just do whatever you think is best, honestly i trust you

turns.agent:
I tried, but Magic Hour refused the generation because your account has **insufficient credits**. No video was created and no credits were spent.

The attempt requested your exact narration, 10 seconds, and no music or on-screen text. I can’t provide a finished download from this attempt.

style.prompt: Use @original as the full visual and timing reference. Reproduce the reference clip's complete 10-second sequence as closely as possible, retaining its subjects, appearance, shot order, camera framing, motion, and pacing. Do not invent extra shots or actions. Add ONLY an off-screen voice-over in warm, clear, approachable English, in a natural conversational adult voice. The narrator must say EXACTLY these words, once, with no additions or omissions: "Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress." Fit the complete narration comfortably within the full 10-second video, beginning promptly, at approximately 144 words per minute. This is voice-over, NOT dialogue: do not animate or synchronize anyone's lips to it. No music, no sound effects, no captions, no subtitles, no titles, no logos, no added on-screen words. Preserve the source's framing as closely as possible within a 16:9 output without stretching subjects. Full duration exactly 10 seconds.
